subject.title: Feature request: first-class Telegram reaction triggers for agent wake-up and execution

question: Should Telegram reaction wake and execution semantics be accepted through the shared `notificationWake.reactions` policy, through a Telegram-specific reaction semantics API, or split across narrower follow-up issues before implementation?
rationale: Current main has passive reaction system events only, and the open candidates add public config/API behavior that affects message delivery and session timing, so automation should not choose the product contract alone.

options.title: Adopt Shared Opt-In Wake Policy
options.body: Use the shared queue/wake/off `notificationWake.reactions` design as the canonical wake path, preserve queued behavior by default, and leave per-emoji execution and durability to narrower follow-ups.

options.title: Sponsor Telegram-Specific Semantics
options.body: Choose a Telegram `reactionSemantics`-style API and require explicit schema/docs/tests plus live Telegram proof before accepting the added config surface.

options.title: Keep The Umbrella Split
options.body: Keep this issue as the Telegram umbrella while narrower issues own cross-channel wake, prompt guidance, custom emoji semantics, and durable persistence independently.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Opt-In Wake Policy
recommendation.body: Use the shared queue/wake/off `notificationWake.reactions` design as the canonical wake path, preserve queued behavior by default, and leave per-emoji execution and durability to narrower follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle owns the open shared-policy candidate and has the strongest current evidence for deciding the config/API direction.
